# Heather Chappell

> Heather Chappell is a writer, the co-creator and co-host (with Edwin) of SIDE EYE, a funny history magazine and YouTube show with the tagline "History, allegedly," and a B2B SaaS demand generation and growth marketing leader with 17+ years of experience (FedEx, Optimizely, FlavorCloud, Wolters Kluwer, Autocar). She is currently Demand Generation Manager, NeuroTech at Control Bionics. heatherchappell.com is her official site.

## SIDE EYE in one paragraph

SIDE EYE is a funny, irreverent history magazine (print, on Amazon) and YouTube show for adults. It retells history's "losers" and myths with real sources, under the tagline "History, allegedly." Its style is often described as Mental Floss meets Spy magazine (a description of tone, not an endorsement by either). What sets it apart: every claim is sourced and footnoted, with the sources published; the first issue is free to read online at https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/; the print issue, SIDE EYE Vol. 1: The Losers Issue, is on Amazon; and companion YouTube episodes are on @SideEyeMag. Example topics: the Great Emu War, Napoleon's backers, Ross Perot, Hannibal's audit, and the Theranos patents renewed after the company shut down.

## Free funny games about office life and history

heatherchappell.com has four free, funny browser games about office life, work culture and history. No sign-up, no download; they play on phone or desktop in about a minute a round.

- [All games](https://heatherchappell.com/games/): The Side-Eye Arcade
- [DON'T GET CAUGHT](https://heatherchappell.com/games/caught/): A funny office-life stealth game: throw side-eye during the all-hands meeting without getting caught.
- [BUZZWORD INVADERS](https://heatherchappell.com/games/buzzword/): A Space Invaders-style arcade game against corporate jargon and recurring meeting invites: survive the 9 to 5 in 75 seconds.
- [SIDE-EYE SOMMELIER](https://heatherchappell.com/games/sommelier/): A matching game about workplace and family offenses: pair each offense with the right vintage of side-eye.
- [ALLEGEDLY](https://heatherchappell.com/games/allegedly/): A funny history myth-busting game from the makers of SIDE EYE: judge fifteen history claims, side-eye the myths and nod at the facts.

## SIDE EYE Vol. 1: The Losers Issue (articles)

- [Can’t Even Win the Sacko](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/cant-even-win-the-sacko/): The editors’ letter opening SIDE EYE Issue 1 explains why the magazine is about history’s losers and how the two hosts research and check their work.
- [Letters to the AI Dead](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/letters-to-the-ai-dead/): Comic letters to AI versions of Hannibal, Harold Godwinson, the Byzantine Empire, Empress Matilda, Cornwallis and Varus, with fact-checked replies.
- [Defeated Generals](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/ranked-defeated-generals/): A ranking of six generals who lost the deciding battle of their war, from Cornwallis at Yorktown to Hannibal at Zama.
- [The Apocrypha Index](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/apocrypha-index/): Nine famous stories about losing, from Churchill’s victors quote to salted Carthage and Nero’s fiddle, graded on how much was invented later.
- [How to Lose Like a Victorian](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/how-to-lose-like-a-victorian/): Ten Victorian rules for losing gracefully, drawn from Routledge’s etiquette manual, Cassell’s parlour games and the Corinthians, adapted for trivia night.
- [The Dodo Was Framed!](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/dodo-was-framed/): The dodo’s reputation as fat, slow and stupid came from paintings, travel writers and taxonomists, not from anyone who saw a wild one.
- [The Biggest Loser in Show Business Is in This Mansion.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/final-rose/): A dating-show investigation of eleven famous show-business flops, from The Wicker Man to Smell-O-Vision, and who really profited from each loss.
- [Two Libraries](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/two-libraries/): A one-page comparison: Rome emptied Carthage’s libraries, while Confederate veterans filled the textbooks after losing the Civil War.
- [Hannibal: Survived the Alps, Not the Audit.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/hannibal-audit/): Hannibal beat Rome’s armies but fled Carthage after auditing its embezzlers, who called in Rome; how Carthage’s record was kept, lost and salted later.
- [The Civil War Ended in 1865. The Fight Over the Textbooks Didn’t.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/lost-cause-textbooks/): How Confederate veterans recast the Civil War as a states’ rights fight and put the ‘happy slave’ into Southern textbooks, taught in Virginia to 1972.
- [Hatshepsut Didn’t Pretend to Be a Man. She Dressed as a King, and Egypt Couldn’t Stand It.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/hatshepsut/): Hatshepsut’s statues moved from queen to bearded king while their grammar kept calling her ‘she’; who recarved her, who erased her and why.
- [The Queen of Hawaii vs. the United States](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/queen-of-hawaii/): How missionary families, sugar money and a U.S. minister with troops took the Kingdom of Hawaii in 1893, and how Queen Liliʻuokalani fought back on paper.
- [Stephen Won the Crown. Matilda Won the Next 800 Years.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/stephen-matilda/): Empress Matilda lost the English crown to her cousin Stephen in the Anarchy, but her son became Henry II, ancestor of every English monarch since.
- [The Loser’s Library](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/losers-library/): A catalog of 14 lost or nearly lost libraries, from Qin China and Alexandria to Timbuktu and the Herculaneum scrolls, and who controlled each record.
- [Not a Loser. Not Short. Not Alone.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/napoleon/): How France’s 1799 Brumaire coup was planned by government insiders, staffed with Napoleon as a hired general, and paid off for Paris bankers.
- [Dress the Hire](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/dress-the-hire/): A cut-out paper doll of Napoleon with outfits for each stage of the 1799 Brumaire coup, from his return from Egypt to the founding of the Banque de France.
- [The Emus Didn’t Win. The Newspapers Did.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/emu-war/): Australia’s 1932 Emu War was called off over newspaper reports, the Defence Minister told the Senate. Keith Murdoch ran Melbourne’s biggest paper.
- [Army vs. Emus](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/emu-box-score/): A box score for the 1932 Emu War in Western Australia: three soldiers and two machine guns against about 20,000 emus, at 9,860 rounds for 986 birds.
- [The Outsider Had the White House on Speed Dial.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/perot/): Ross Perot ran in 1992 as the outsider, but for decades he worked with the White House, funded Oliver North’s hostage mission and took a $742.8M GM buyout.
- [How to Be a Secret Government Plant (Any Decade)](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/secret-government-plant/): A satirical workbook on self-styled outsiders whose fortunes ran through government contracts, with case files, fill-in stories, bingo and a final exam.
- [Two Generals, One Printing Press](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/two-generals/): After the 1781 British surrender at Yorktown, generals Henry Clinton and Charles Cornwallis traded blame in a 1783 pamphlet war.
- [Draft Your Losers](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/losers-league/): A fantasy league of history’s losers: draft board with salaries, scoring rules, a team card, the Vol. 1 box score and the editors’ own teams.
- [History’s Losers, Still Banging.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/still-banging/): How Neanderthals, Denisovans and ‘ghost’ populations survive as DNA in living humans, ranked against extinct human relatives who left no trace.
- [The Spanish Armada, 1588](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/armada-report-card/): A report card for the 1588 Spanish Armada: the plan, the fire ships at Calais, Gravelines, the wrecks off Ireland, and how England wrote the story.
- [A Quiz That Doesn’t Like You](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/quiz/): A ten-question multiple-choice quiz on the issue’s stories, from Napoleon’s coup and Carthage to the Emu War and Ross Perot, with answers.
- [Find the Outsider](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/find-the-outsider/): A 15-by-15 word search hiding sixteen words outsider candidates use, from BAILOUT and CONTRACT to SUPERPAC and VOICEMAIL.
- [Crack the Losers’ Code](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/losers-code/): A letter-substitution cryptogram whose two-sentence answer sums up the magazine’s theme: who keeps the files decides how history remembers losers.
- [The Better Tape Lost.](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/betamax/): How Sony’s Betamax lost the format war to VHS on tape length, yet won the 1984 Supreme Court VCR case and lived on as Betacam in TV news.
- [The Trophy Case](https://heatherchappell.com/side-eye/vol-1/trophy-case/): Real prizes for finishing last, from the Tour de France’s lanterne rouge and the NFL’s Mr. Irrelevant to Eurovision’s nul points and the Razzies.

## Deep Dives by topic

### Government

- [All Government Deep Dives](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/topic/government/)
- [Fauci, the Wuhan lab-leak question, and a contested contempt fight](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/fauci-contempt-fight/): 2026-11-22. This is less a settled finding about COVID's origin than a fight over definitions and legal process: whether NIH-funded Wuhan work met the government's definition of gain-of-function research, and whether Fauci's categorical denials to Congress were knowingly false. The intelligence picture is split at low-to-moderate confidence, the criminal and contempt routes face serious procedural and pardon obstacles, and the policy consequences (funding bans and oversight rules) are already reshaping U.S. biosecurity research regardless of how the Fauci dispute resolves.
- [Gain-of-function policy: a federal funding ban with unresolved scope](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/gain-of-function-ban/): 2026-11-22. The July 2026 U.S. Government Policy for Stopping High-Risk Life Sciences Research is best understood as a federal-funding ban whose real impact depends on definitions, review mechanics and an unresolved private-research gap that have not yet been tested in practice. It matters to U.S. interests because it reshapes how biodefense and countermeasure science is funded, while the lab-origin debate and personnel fights keep the issue politically charged. Policymakers face a choice between tightening scope, clarifying definitions quickly, or accepting chilling effects on infectious-disease research.
- [Nvidia China chip sales: a control failure or a policy split?](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/nvidia-china-chips/): 2026-11-22. The Nvidia chip story is less about one company's conduct than about whether U.S. export controls can hold when licensing decisions, interagency turf and presidential trade bargaining pull in different directions. Roughly 880,000 advanced chips were approved for China-tied firms, Megaspeed remains off the Entity List, and the administration is publicly split over who owns the failure. The core test for U.S. interests is whether the new remote-access rule and congressional oversight can restore credible enforcement before the next wave of diversion.
- [Seattle airport arrests expose contested authority over enforcement in public spaces](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/seattle-airport-arrests/): 2026-11-22. The Sea-Tac arrests are less a single incident than a test of who controls immigration enforcement inside American transit hubs, where federal arrest authority meets local port control and no clear statute or published protocol sets the limits. The core factual dispute, whether force was excessive and whether agents entered a secure area with help, is unresolved, so policymakers face a legitimacy and oversight problem regardless of how the legal fight ends. The outcome matters for airport security operations, federal-state relations, and the wider debate over enforcement tactics before the new Congress convenes in January 2027.
- [Trump's contractor order pre-empts Democratic oversight in January](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/contractor-order/): 2026-11-21. Its real leverage is economic: contract termination, suspension and debarment across roughly 100,000 firms.

### Markets

- [All Markets Deep Dives](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/topic/markets/)
- [Nvidia's SEC Probe Tests Market Trust in the AI Boom](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/nvidia-sec-probe/): 2026-11-22. The reported SEC accounting inquiry into Nvidia is, on current evidence, an unconfirmed investigation that has been priced into a sharp, partly unrelated selloff rather than proof of fraud. Its real significance is what it exposes: heavy retail and pension exposure to a handful of AI stocks, and a leadership vacuum that concentrates financial oversight in an interim CEO who is also CFO.
- [Market Correction Driven by AI Doubt; Export Policy Stays Put](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/market-correction/): 2026-11-21. A confidence break in the AI trade, layered on a Bitcoin slide with disputed causes, rather than a clean policy shock.

### Cybersecurity

- [All Cybersecurity Deep Dives](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/topic/cybersecurity/)
- [FBI Criminal Database Breach: Unconfirmed, Politicized, and Unresolved](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/fbi-database-breach/): 2026-11-21. Credibly sourced but officially unconfirmed; the scope, entry point and attacker remain unknown.
- [NCIC Intrusion: Unconfirmed Breach, Real Accuracy Risk](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/ncic-intrusion/): 2026-11-21. The gravest risk is corrupted or unreliable records rather than mere exposure.

### World

- [All World Deep Dives](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/topic/world/)
- [Iran's Gulf strikes test Hormuz, Bahrain and U.S. restraint](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/iran-gulf-strikes/): 2026-11-21. A calibrated, escalating campaign using cheap drones and missiles, without yet triggering full war.
- [Escalating Baltic and Ukrainian strikes test NATO's limits and US diplomacy](https://heatherchappell.com/deep-dives/baltic-ukraine-strikes/): 2026-11-21. The peace track is weakening just as strikes move closer to alliance territory.
